sources.entry: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in R by Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, and Robert Tibshirani

summary.name: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
summary.one_liner: A broad, less technical textbook on statistical learning methods, with R and Python lab sections in each chapter.
use_cases: following R or Python lab exercises
studying survival analysis and unsupervised learning
summary.what_it_does: The page describes An Introduction to Statistical Learning, a book giving a broad, less technical treatment of key statistical learning topics for anyone who wants to use contemporary data analysis tools. The chapters cover regression, classification, resampling, linear model selection and regularization, moving beyond linearity, tree-based methods, support vector machines, deep learning, survival analysis, unsupervised learning, and multiple testing. Each edition includes an end-of-chapter lab that demonstrates the concepts in either R or Python. The first edition (ISLR) came out in 2013, a second edition in 2021, and the Python edition (ISLP) in 2023. The page says the book has been translated into several languages.
notable: Lab at the end of each chapter in R or Python
Available in R (ISLR) and Python (ISLP) editions
Translated into Chinese, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Mongolian, Russian, and Vietnamese
caveats: The page does not state pricing or how to obtain the book
